sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from the observed binary-instrument experiment with fixed \(\pi_z>0\).
sampling_model.overlap: Instrument arms have positive probabilities; treatment overlap outside \([p_0,p_1]\) is not imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional multinomial cell probabilities are estimated by armwise empirical proportions and projected onto \(\overline{\mathcal Q}\cap E\) only for the certified regular branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Uniformly sharp rank-similar counterfactual-average bounds rely on full complier support.
Aumann-expectation identification regions admit Hausdorff-consistent estimation and set-valued limit theory.
Criterion-minimizer identified sets admit Hausdorff-rate and confidence-region analysis.
Test inversion can cover an entire identified set uniformly under stated conditions.
Ordinary-bootstrap validity under Gaussian limits is equivalent to full Hadamard differentiability.
Calibrated projection gives uniformly valid intervals for smooth functions in moment-inequality models.
Sharp treatment-effect-distribution bounds can have nonstandard limits and ordinary-bootstrap failure.
Categorical instrumental-variable compatibility and confidence inversion reduce to finite convex programs.
Discrete structural instrumental-variable functions are generally set identified and support sensitive.

body.tldr: A binary instrument identifies complier outcome distributions but policies below \(p_0\) and above \(p_1\) require extrapolation. Under exactly Marx's existential rank similarity and a fixed finite ordered outcome alphabet, the sharp simultaneous policy-mean set is a finite nonconvex union of common-rank path images, each attained by one law. This finite-alphabet missing-support class and Marx's full-support class are nonnested; the reduction to Marx applies only on their finite-alphabet full-support overlap, and the observable monotonicity inequalities are derived from the latent model. Path survival gives the exact Hausdorff continuity frontier and a centered local Lipschitz bound. A legal three-outcome contiguous submodel proves that globally honest metric procedures cannot shrink uniformly. A terminating finite algorithm computes the multinomial outer set, the set-of-sets image, and their exact Hausdorff radii; finite-sample coverage is the direct inversion corollary. On every certified continuity law, the full projected Hausdorff-loss germ is recovered pointwise on the exact multinomial sampling face, including continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero faces; this requires positive instrument shares and does not imply globally shrinking honest metric inference.

project_justification.gap: Marx's full-support condition makes rank-similar groupwise extrema jointly attainable. Within the fixed finite-alphabet setting, allowing missing complier support leaves no published sharp joint policy-grid set, no stability criterion for disappearing common-rank couplings, and no finite procedure computing Hausdorff radii for the resulting set-of-sets inversion.
project_justification.niche: Finite outcomes convert existential common ranks into finitely many ordered chains, but the resulting set is a law-dependent nonconvex union rather than one convex program or one smooth projection.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the observable compatibility inequalities from the maintained latent model and supplies a sharp path-union representation, finite exclusion certificates, an if-and-only-if continuity frontier, a contiguous impossibility theorem, a terminating exact inversion-and-radius algorithm, the accompanying finite-sample coverage corollary, and pointwise projected full-loss Gaussian calibration at every certified continuity law on its exact multinomial sampling face. The calibration covers continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero faces, requires positive instrument shares, and makes no uniform calibration or globally shrinking honest metric-inference claim. The finite-alphabet missing-support class and Marx's full-support class are nonnested, with the Marx reduction confined to their finite-alphabet full-support overlap.

body.related_work: Marx (2024) is the direct substantive anchor: Proposition 5 obtains uniformly sharp rank-similar policy bounds under full complier support, and footnote 29 identifies the construction that fails without it. The present finite-alphabet missing-support class and Marx's full-support class are nonnested; the reduction to Proposition 5 applies only on their finite-alphabet full-support overlap. Imbens and Rubin (1997) give the principal-stratum interpretation underlying the observable monotonicity inequalities; here those inequalities are derived as compatibility checks. Chesher (2010), Torgovitsky (2019), and Han and Yang (2024) show how discrete structural restrictions can be encoded by finite feasibility or linear programs; they inform the allocation representation but do not impose one common ordered rank across every latent-index bin. Beresteanu and Molinari (2008) and Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer (2007) provide regular Hausdorff theory for different set-valued substrates; the survival theorem addresses law-dependent component death in a nonconvex union. Romano and Shaikh (2010) motivate the coverage corollary through general identified-set inversion. Song et al. (2026) informs the finite categorical feasibility layer, while the algorithm theorem adds common-parameter nonconvex unions and exact outer-set and hyperspace Hausdorff radii. Fang and Santos (2019), Kaido, Molinari, and Stoye (2019), and Fan and Park (2010) motivate nonsmooth set-valued calibration; here the complete projected Hausdorff-loss germ is recovered pointwise at every certified continuity law on its exact multinomial sampling face, including continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero faces, under positive instrument shares but without a uniform-calibration claim.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The projected full Hausdorff-loss germ is solved pointwise, including at continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero sampling faces. The result remains conditional on a certified continuity law, positive instrument shares, and correct specification of the exact multinomial sampling face. It is not uniform over laws or faces, and a path-domain-only bootstrap still does not suffice because the full loss may change affine pieces while every path domain remains unchanged. None of these local calibration conclusions defeats the contiguous discontinuity obstruction to globally shrinking honest Hausdorff inference.
body.honest_scope: The path representation is scoped to a fixed finite outcome alphabet. That missing-support class and Marx's full-support class are nonnested, and the reduction to Marx's Proposition 5 holds only on their finite-alphabet full-support overlap. The inequalities \(c_0\ge0\) and \(c_1\ge0\) are derived observed-law compatibility checks, not maintained assumptions. The finite survival criterion, centered Lipschitz implication, three-outcome discontinuity, impossibility argument, and exact finite inversion-and-radius algorithm are theorem-level results. Simultaneous finite-sample coverage is a direct corollary of observed-law coverage and inversion, with no finite-sample optimality claim. Projected full-loss Gaussian calibration is solved pointwise at every certified continuity law on the exact multinomial sampling face, including continuous multi-path switches, propensity--grid ties, and exact lower-dimensional structural-zero faces; it requires positive instrument shares and the exact face. Pairwise-neighborhood Lipschitz continuity, a globally continuous derivative, uniform calibration, and globally shrinking honest Hausdorff inference are not claimed. The one-path folded-normal law is a check and special case of the general active-germ theorem. For \(K=2\), only the two monotone paths remain.
